subject: OrbitEdge migration: GPU capacity pact, validation & cutover governance
messages:
From: Cory Mills <cory@orbitedge.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@orbitedge.ai, elaine.zhou@orbitedge.ai
Date: 2025-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration: high-level asks and target windows

Hi Naomi / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. OrbitEdge is ready to move from hosted API to a dedicated footprint for our production traffic, and procurement asked me to capture the immediate asks so we can align timelines. High-level items we need from Redwood: 

- A firm (non-binding) capacity proposal for the first 90 days post-swap (GPU count + expected peak RPS/token throughput).
- Validation plan: staged smoke/canary windows, acceptance criteria, and rollback triggers.
- Proposed cutover dates (we're targeting late Nov / early Dec) and blackout windows.
- Any staging access we can have to run load and synthetic tests (test keys / endpoints).
- Draft MRA so procurement can start an initial review.

Also: OrbitEdge would like to understand burst capacity options (short-term > committed) and any onboarding credits you can offer given the 12-month commitment we're discussing.

Would appreciate a single doc we can circulate to legal/procurement. Can you get that over by EOD Tuesday PST?

—Cory
Cory Mills
Head of Platform, OrbitEdge
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Cory Mills <cory@orbitedge.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration: high-level asks and target windows

Cory —

Thanks — attaching a concise package for procurement and the ops leads. At a high level:

Executive summary (draft):
- Initial pledge: 12 virtual A100-equivalents (vA100) for staging + canary (reserved but idle until staging run).
- Committed production baseline: 24 vA100-equivalents (monthly reserved capacity) with the ability to burst +8 vA100 for short windows (billing at burst rate).
- Expected performance: with our standard batching and KV prefix caching, we expect sustained throughput of ~1.8M tokens/min at p50 latency <100ms for common completion sizes; p95 latency target 150ms under normal load.

Proposed validation & cutover timeline (draft):
- Week -2 (staging prep): shared staging keys, mirror traffic baseline, run synthetic stress up to 60% of target RPS.
- Week -1 (canary phase): 10% traffic routed to dedicated for 24–48 hours; run user acceptance prompts and regressions.
- Cutover day: ramp to 50% over first 12 hours, 100% after 48 hours subject to acceptance gates.
- Rollback window: first 72 hours post-100% — automatic fallback policy to hosted on sustained error rate >2% or p95 latency >500ms for more than 10 minutes.

Acceptance gates (short list):
- Throughput validation: sustained RPS within ±15% of model used in capacity workbook (attached).
- Latency: p95 ≤150ms for the agreed prompt set (we'll import your prompt set into our eval harness).
- Quality: no regression on the 50-case prompt set (quality delta ≤2% on your scoring).

Attachments: Orbitedge_MRA_draft.pdf (procurement), orbitedge_capacity_model.xlsx (workbook with assumed token mix and RPS).

I added Ben and Karthik on the thread for the technical sizing and the acceptance criteria. We'll iterate quickly — can push a DocuSign link for the MRA as soon as procurement confirms the draft is close.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OrbitEdge migration: GPU capacity pact, validation & cutover governance

Naomi — quick sizing comments for the capacity workbook (referenced in Naomi's email).

Notes:
- The \"vA100-equivalent\" numbers assume our quantized LLM runtime (int8 paths) for the primary model family. If OrbitEdge requires fp16 or larger sequence lengths we should add +25% headroom.
- For 24 vA100 baseline: recommend layout across 3 racks (8 devices/rack) to avoid single-rack blast radius and to give us per-region failover options during cutover.
- Canary config: live KV caching warmup takes ~3–4 minutes per sustained user—plan the first canary window for low traffic hours and include cold-cache probes in the acceptance tests.
- Cost note: committed monthly baseline + burst pricing is in the MRA draft. We can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $15k if the deal signs before Dec 15.

Quick ask to internal team: confirm the rollback automation owner (ops runbook) and the trace sampling rate we'll enable for the canary (I suggest 10% sampled traces).

Ben
Head of Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-11-15T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OrbitEdge migration: GPU capacity pact, validation & cutover governance

Cory / Team —

Adding the acceptance criteria and test endpoints you'll use to validate capacity during the staging and canary windows. Please share a short list (5–10) of representative prompts and the scoring rubric so we can lock quality gates.

Acceptance & test plan (technical):
- Endpoints: staging.llm.redwood-internal.com:443 (staging key), canary.llm.redwood-internal.com:443 (canary key).
- Load scenarios: 1) baseline steady RPS (30 min), 2) 3x burst (10 min) to validate throttle/burst behavior, 3) simulated cold-cache ramp (30 min).
- Metrics we will capture: token throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate, model output similarity scores (oracle), GPU utilization and mem pressure per rack.
- Rollback triggers (automated): sustained error rate >2% for 15m OR p95 latency >500ms for 10m OR quality drift >3% on the eval prompt set.
- Manual gate: post-canary runbook review with OrbitEdge app owners — explicit signoff required before moving to >50% traffic.

DocuSign: Naomi, I've uploaded the MRA draft and added the technical addendum; DocuSign link is in the attachments list. Procurement can start review using that link.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime and Ops

--
Karthik's internal note: Set trace sampling to 10% for canary, 1% post-cutover for cost control. Ops runbook owner: Marissa for primary, Ben backup.

Thanks everyone — this looks good and aligns with our internal calendar. A few quick confirmations before procurement signs: 

1) Canary window: we'd like Nov 29 02:00–Nov 30 06:00 PST for the first canary (low traffic window). Confirmed?
2) Burst capacity: confirm ability to +8 vA100 for up to 4 hours without long lead time.
3) Onboarding credit: we'll take the $15k credit if the MRA signs before Dec 15.
4) DocuSign: Elaine in procurement will route the MRA; procure@orbitedge.ai is on CC.

If you can confirm items (1) and (2) today, we'll lock internal calendar invites and start the procurement review.

—Cory
Cory Mills
Head of Platform, OrbitEdge
